tasks.short: Coordinate actual judges' meeting and appointment schedules

steps.what: Locate and read actual judges' calendars, appointment requests and participant availability using native calendar views
inputs: Actual appointment requests and existing calendar availability
outputs: Actual available times, request details and unresolved conflicts

steps.what: Coordinate actual priorities, constraints and appointment choices with the judge and participants and capture the agreed details
inputs: Actual requests, availability and conflicts from s1
outputs: Actual agreed and captured meeting time, location, participants and purpose

steps.what: Write the actual shared-calendar entry and check its complete details, reusing exact already captured request fields in native calendar fields
inputs: Actual agreed details captured in s2
Exact request fields read in s1
outputs: Complete actual calendar entry checked for time, location, participants and agreement

steps.what: Save the actual completed entry to the existing shared calendar without issuing an invitation or separate notice
inputs: Actual completed calendar entry from s3

tasks.design: Configure native {CALENDAR} availability views and exact request-field reuse for actual appointment coordination. Keep priorities, participant discussion and complete calendar-entry writing and checking human, with an ordinary ungated same-system save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating actual availability and repeating already agreed appointment fields can interrupt scheduling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native shared calendars can show actual availability and reuse exact request fields.
tasks.still_hard: The judge's priorities and real participant constraints require actual agreement.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicts with the people concerned and preserve the actual agreement.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native shared calendars support availability views and exact appointment fields while priority decisions and participant agreement remain human.

assumptions: This conditional episode uses an existing shared-calendar entry following actual participant coordination. Shares are illustrative, not measured or based on the supplied prior.

Actual requests and calendars are existing sources. The clerk reads and verifies them in s1 and actually obtains and captures agreed details in s2. No free clean availability feed or automatically inferred judge priority is assumed.
Use native calendar features first. Already available views and field reuse are baseline and earn no additional gain. Actual conflicts and missing information require retained conversation.

s3 includes actual entry writing and ordinary completeness checking, not a new approval ceremony. The author does not approve their own work. The separate same-system save has no self-gate, is negligible today and earns no saving; 1 is the schema's minimum positive integer allocation.

This episode updates an existing shared calendar with notifications disabled. If the real workflow sends an invitation or notice, include that separate actual send and its genuine final-version authority rather than hiding it in the save.
unknowns: Actual calendar settings and duplicate request-field effort
research_questions: Observe actual appointment coordination and distinguish shared-calendar recording from any invitation send.

already_counted.description: Remaining source work, actual participant coordination and complete calendar-entry writing and checking remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain availability access and exact request-field mappings.

outputs: Actual human conference participation and captured required note content

Actual case identifiers selected in s1

tasks.design: Configure native {OTHER} case views and exact case fields in the actual {DOCS} working note. Retain conference participation, substantive note writing and ordinary source checking, followed by an ungated same-system save.

tasks.enabler_now: Native case views and fixed fields can reuse actual selected records without interpreting the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: The meaning and consequences of the actual legal discussion require human understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Follow the conference and distinguish a proposal, unresolved point and actual decision.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: case views and exact document fields can reduce source lookup and identifier entry while legal discussion and substantive working notes remain human.

assumptions: This illustrative episode actually requires an existing conference working note. Do not invent a report after every discussion or extrapolate this mix to all conferences; shares are not measured or based on the prompt prior.
Actual source reading remains in s1 and actual conference content is produced and captured in s2. Only exact case-field reuse reduces s3; all substantive writing and meaning checks remain human.
Use native tools first; existing case views and fields are baseline. No transcript, judge's order, legal conclusion or model-written record is assumed.
